title: Bounded Defect Layer Optimization with Mirror Regularization
scientific_hypothesis: Constraining the defect layer (index 10) physical thickness to 480-550 nm range while applying soft regularization on mirror layers (indices 0-9, 11-20) will stabilize the cavity resonance condition and prevent the score regression observed in iterations 4-5, enabling the optimizer to converge on the correct half-wave optical thickness near 750 nm at 1550 nm.
design_principle: Quarter-wave mirror stacks bracketing a half-wave defect cavity, with explicit bounds on defect thickness to guide resonance formation while allowing mirror fine-tuning for stopband performance.
proposed_topology: 21-layer fixed sequence: HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2(defect)|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2 on fused silica substrate, air incident
design_variables: Mirror layers 0-9 and 11-20 thickness with L2 regularization toward quarter-wave values
soft_objectives: Minimize thickness deviation from quarter-wave optical thickness in mirrors
manufacturing_considerations: Defect layer thickness range compatible with standard deposition control
theory_basis: Fabry-Perot cavity resonance requires half-wave optical thickness at target wavelength
Quarter-wave stack provides high reflectance stopband when index contrast is sufficient
expected_advantages: Bounded defect prevents optimizer from exploring non-resonant thickness regimes
Mirror regularization maintains stopband performance while cavity is tuned
Directly addresses feedback directive on defect layer reinitialization
known_risks: Bounds may be too restrictive if optimal defect thickness lies outside 480-550 nm
Regularization may prevent mirror layers from adapting to actual cavity condition
execution_request_english: Optimize a 21-layer HfO2/SiO2 defect cavity stack on fused silica substrate at normal incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2(defect)|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2. Constrain layer 10 (defect, HfO2) physical thickness to 480-550 nm range. Apply L2 regularization penalty on layers 0-9 and 11-20 toward quarter-wave optical thickness at 1550 nm. Maximize transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band and reflectance in 400-700 nm band. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with bounded constraints. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Maximum 30 layers.
revision_reason: Iteration 4-5 score regression (0.7731 to 0.7611 to 0.7654) suggests cavity resonance drift. Feedback directive specifies defect layer reinitialization in 480-550 nm range with mirror regularization to prevent excessive drift while establishing correct cavity optical thickness.
